textbookText: Pheretima posthuma Observe the animal given below and answer the following questions.

i. What might be its phylum and scientific name? ii. This animal always keeps skin moist? Why? iii. Is it free living or parasitic? iv. What might be its white coloured thick band near the anterior end of body? v. Is it beneficial for us? How?
Kingdom Phylum Class Genus Species Common name
: Animalia : Annelida : Oligochaeta : Pheretima : posthuma : Earthworm

The animal shown in the diagram is earthworm belonging to the phylum annelida and its scientific name is Pheretima posthuma. Earthworms are found under the soil in moist burrow. They have not developed any special respiratory organs like lungs, gills or other structures and hence they respire through moist skin. They maintain skin moist with the help of mucous glands present in their skin. Such type of respiration is called cutaneous respiration. They are free living and omnivorous animals. They feed on soil rich in decaying organic matter, dried leaves, insect larva, protozoans, arthropod exoskeleton etc. Nearer to the anterior end, their body contains a ring or belt like conspicious glandular tissue called clitellum which forms cocoons. Earthworms are useful in agriculture as they help to increase the fertility of soil by their movements and excreta, hence considered friend of farmers.

8.3.2 HABIT AND HABITAT Earthworms are terrestrial, living in burrows and moist soil rich in decaying organic matters. They are mostly found under the soil in irrigated farmlands, garden, lawns etc. They are free living and nocturnal animals. At night time, they come out of their burrow for searching food, finding new habitat and for reproductive activities. Similarly, they are seen in large number on the earth surface during rainy season as it is their breeding season and burrows are full of water due to heavy rainfall. Earthworm makes burrow by excavating and engulfing soil with its

anterior end and moving down progressively. It derives food from decaying organic matter present in the soil and discharge the undigested content along with the soil as faecal matter in the form of “worm casting”. Although they are hermaphrodite, self-fertilization does not occur. Hence, there always occurs copulation between two mature worms. In earthworm copulation is for the exchange of sperm between two mature worms. Fertilization is external that takes place in cocoon and development is direct. Earthworms also have capacity to reproduce asexually by regeneration. 8.3.3 EXTERNAL FEATURES (MORPHOLOGY) Activity 8.7 Objective: To identify the external parts of an earthworm Apparatus required: dissecting tray, foreceps, needle Procedure: i. Take a freshly caught or preserved specimen of earthworm. (Kill the freshly caught earthworm by dipping it in formalin) ii. Then, Keep it on dissecting tray. iii. Point out its external parts with the needle. (Take the help of your teacher if required) iv. Note down all the structures on white board. v. Now discuss its external characteristics and draw its well labeled diagram. Conclusion 1. Shape, size and colour Body of Pheretima is vermiform, elongated, cylindrical and bilaterally symmetrical. It is pointed anteriorly and more or less blunt posteriorly. A mature earthworm measures about 15 cm in length and 0.3-0.5 cm in diameter. Body colour of earthworm is shining deep brown because of the presence of porphyrin pigment in the body wall. This pigment also protects the body from the harmful effect of solar radiations. Dorsal surface is darker than ventral surface and carries dorsal blood vessel as a median line from the anterior end to the posterior end. 2. Segmentation Body of earthworm is soft which is divided into 100-120 similar segments called somites or metameres. Segments are separated externally by grooves and internally by septa. Segmentation is true because external segmentation corresponds with internal segmentation which is called metamerism, hence its body is metamerically segmented. 3. Prostomium and peristomium The anterior part of the earthworm is not differentiated as a distinct head and without sense organs like eyes, tentacles. The first segment of the earthworm in which mouth is situated called peristomium (peri-around; stoma-mouth). From the peristomium arises anteriorly, a fleshy lobe-like structure called the prostomium (pro-before; stoma-mouth). Prostomium is also called the boring organ and it is tactile organ too.
